clue.text: Acquire new owners, giving a little money to staff

parts.note: loose coins are called change
workers or crew are hands, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: A business is sold, with the new owners slipping some cash to the employees.
explanation.definitionFit: When property is sold it passes to a new owner, the idiom being that it moves between holders.

clue.text: Arrogant male joining firm

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
firm in the sense of certain, sure

explanation.surface: A swaggering man who joins a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Overconfident and conceited, synonym.

clue.text: One stays unemotional about a high honour

indicators.note: stays as in supports, holding the other letters within

parts.note: an ace is a one on dice or cards

indicators.note: about means surrounding the letter

parts.note: cold means lacking warmth or feeling

explanation.surface: One person remains impassive about receiving a great honour.
explanation.walkthrough: COLD goes about A to give COLAD, which ACE then holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or praise of distinction, as when a knighthood is conferred.

clue.text: Such important people associated with good Hurrah!

definitions.text: Such important people associated with good
definitions.meaning: 'the ... and the good' are the eminent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the great and the good' names eminent figures; and an exclamation of delight means hooray.

clue.text: Not coming clean, doing farm work?

explanation.definitionFit: Evasive equivocation; also cutting and laying the hedgerows on a farm.

clue.text: In the home, live very close

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
to live is to be, as in 'we are'

explanation.surface: Living in the house right next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of near: closest.

clue.text: Professional soldiers thus allowed to go over the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over places these pieces above the soldiers

parts.note: so means thus
licit means lawful, allowed
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Career troops are permitted to leave the trenches and charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over the top' evokes soldiers charging from trenches; here it means the first pieces stand above the soldiers in the down light. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer is a member of a profession.

clue.text: Negligible amount of fruit

definitions.meaning: 'not worth a ...' means of no value at all
a soft sweet fruit of the Mediterranean

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a trifling quantity is a fig; also the familiar sweet fruit eaten fresh or dried.

clue.text: Splendour of noon in really hot surroundings

indicators.note: in places the letter within the other word
surroundings tells us the hot word encloses the letter

parts.note: fiery means blazing, very hot

explanation.surface: Midday splendour amid a scorching landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy clothing or decoration, splendid attire.

clue.text: Demand being accepted, receive seal

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: to receive is to get
to demand is to ask

explanation.surface: A request is approved and a seal of approval follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber or fibre ring used as a seal between joined surfaces.

clue.text: Set of songs that may transport one

definitions.meaning: a song ... is a linked group of songs

explanation.definitionFit: A song series performed together is so named; and the word is short for a bicycle, which carries a rider.

clue.text: Late with some writing missing these?

definitions.text: Late with some writing missing these?

parts.note: late in the sense of deceased
lines are rows of writing, or a school punishment of written lines

explanation.surface: A writer who is late with their copy has missed the cut-off dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as tardy, but in the wordplay it means deceased; the whole clue then describes what a late writer misses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tardy writer misses the time limits set for delivering copy.

clue.text: Gem of a computer game

definitions.meaning: a diamond set on its own in a ring
the single-player card game bundled with Windows

explanation.definitionFit: A single precious stone mounted alone takes this name, as does the patience card game long shipped on PCs.

clue.text: Swear miracle perhaps involved saint

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a miraculous healing is one kind of cure

explanation.surface: Someone blasphemes about a miracle in which a saint played a part.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to utter an oath or profanity, synonym for the verb.

clue.text: High-flyer to wed anew, putting appropriate article on

indicators.note: putting the article on the other letters means it is worn round them like a band

parts.note: a ring is the fitting item for a wedding

indicators.note: anew means made again in a new form, so the letters of wed are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambitious person remarries and puts on the right accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests an ambitious go-getter, but it is a bird; 'putting ... on' pictures slipping the ring round the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush that visits Britain in winter is a bird, a literal flyer in the sky.

clue.text: Pay rise popular with union? About right

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word wraps the letter

parts.note: cement is a bond or union

explanation.surface: A trade union welcomes a pay award as fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but means a bond, CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular step up in salary on a pay scale.

clue.text: Picture-house to announce cancelled opening

indicators.note: the opening letter is struck out of the word

parts.note: to state is to declare or announce

explanation.surface: A cinema declares that its premiere has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture-house' suggests a cinema, but here it is the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: London's national art galleries house paintings, so they are literally buildings for pictures.

clue.text: Food consumed in the tube

parts.note: reads as eating on the London Underground, but describes pasta shaped as tubes

explanation.definitionFit: A pasta made in short hollow pipes.

clue.text: Greet sea, having travelled in this once?

definitions.text: Greet sea, having travelled in this once?

indicators.note: travelled means moved about, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A poor emigrant meeting the ocean on a voyage below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having travelled' rearranges GREET SEA; the whole clue pictures the cheapest class of passage on old liners.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest passenger accommodation on old ships, in which emigrants crossed the ocean.

clue.text: Swindle as son joins academic stream

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A con trick in which a boy enrols at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river at Cambridge, England's university town.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud or con is synonymous with the noun.

clue.text: Trough engulfs a boss

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the trough holds the letter

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough for animals

explanation.surface: A feeding trough swallows the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of staff, synonym.

clue.text: Dropping off at the start, porter's time for sleeping

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a doorman is a porter at a building's entrance

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of the word off

explanation.surface: A night porter nodding off at the beginning of his shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The O that starts 'off' is dropped from DOORMAN, leaving DORMAN, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An inactive, resting state, as of a volcano or animal in hibernation.

clue.text: Jog to keep close to subversive

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: Running beside a political agitator.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy steady trot, a gentle run.

clue.text: Knocked timidly, being taken advantage of

definitions.meaning: exploited, as when a resource is drawn upon

explanation.definitionFit: Gave a soft rap; also exploited or drawn on, as in a phone line or an asset.

clue.text: Equipment given to school is tasteless stuff

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A school receives a gift of tacky gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy or sentimental art, admired ironically.

clue.text: Child principally involved in a story

definitions.text: Child principally involved in a story

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the other letters

parts.note: a story is a fib, a lie

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of Child

explanation.surface: A girl who is the main character in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits inside A LIE; the whole clue describes Lewis Carroll's heroine of Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's young girl is the heroine of the Wonderland books.

clue.text: Get money for treat

definitions.meaning: to cash a cheque or bill
to treat with is to bargain or discuss terms

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is to convert a cheque into cash; the other is to bargain or hold talks.

clue.text: One going ahead to question enemy leader

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of enemy

explanation.surface: A scout goes in front to interrogate the enemy chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going ahead' reads as advancing; it means going on a head, as a hat does.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall white chef's hat, worn on the head.

clue.text: Travellers to proceed, with change to green

definitions.note: the definition is plural, the answer singular, though it can refer collectively

parts.note: to pass is to go on or proceed

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of green are rearranged

explanation.surface: Road users are told to move on as the light turns green.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding in a vehicle without driving it is a traveller on board.

clue.text: Hear one repeating exactly how much you have to do

definitions.text: how much you have to do

indicators.note: hear signals that the word is to be listened to, not spelt

parts.note: someone who repeats another's words is a quoter

explanation.surface: A listener who parrots exactly the amount of work assigned.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech QUOTER and QUOTA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An assigned share or target of work.

clue.text: Note expressing exasperation with Homer?

definitions.meaning: the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa's first scale degree; also the cartoon father Homer Simpson's cry of annoyance.

clue.text: Hint, uttered mysteriously is to effect major reversal

indicators.note: mysteriously means in a puzzling way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clue whispered cryptically that changes everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' rearranges the letters of HINT UTTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from the sea's ebb and flow: to reverse the course of events.
